memory.text: The user is an executive assistant.
The user is in the Pacific time zone (PT/PST).

Preferred format for exec conference-room rundowns: markdown table, full day chronological, BOLD meetings that need a room. Columns: time | meeting | booked | preferred-room-A | preferred-room-B. Use ✅ free / ❌ taken / ⚠️ partial for the room columns.

Exec conference-room booking logic: (1) prefer small preferred rooms to avoid hogging scarce large rooms; (2) cluster back-to-back meetings into ONE room; a new cluster is fine in a different room if there is a >=1hr break; (3) NEVER make the exec switch floors when there is no break between calls; (4) when a large call already has a big room booked, book the meeting right after in a small room on the SAME floor.
Room-rundown automation should always be 2 BUSINESS DAYS ahead (Mon→Wed, Tue→Thu, Wed→Fri, Thu→next Mon, Fri→next Tue). Runs weekdays only.
Room-rundown checks FIRST if the exec is WFH/traveling/OOO that day (all-day event, WFH, traveling, working-location=Home, PTO); if so post a one-line remote note and skip the chart.
The supported exec prefers taking meetings from conference rooms instead of their desk.
Leadership-outreach Slack channel posts requests for execs to reach out; the EA reacts ✅ to ones already sent. Track per-exec sent vs outstanding in a Notion or sheet tracker.
When drafting emails or messages on the user's behalf, never use em dashes; they look AI-generated.
Never send email or Slack on the user's behalf without them reading and approving the exact draft first. Draft only until they say to send.
Prefer Google Calendar and Gmail MCP connectors over the box browser when available; browser SSO can be flaky.
Prefer request sheets sorted by recency, with the newest requests at the top.
Prefer emoji tapbacks instead of a text reply when no real response is needed (thanks, got it, casual ack).
For exec room bookings, prefer keeping large staff/forecast/leadership calls out of the smallest preferred rooms; keep those small rooms for 1:1s and smaller meetings when possible.

routines.description: Weekdays: check today's interviews vs a Notion prep doc. (routine; starts paused until its placeholders are filled)

files.SKILL.md:
---
name: Exec interview-prep reminder
description: >-
  Weekdays: check today's interviews vs a Notion prep doc.
schedule: 0 8 * * 1-5
timezone: {timezone}
paused: true
---
Weekday (Mon–Fri) morning task. Goal: make sure the supported exec has prep for every interview TODAY (user local timezone).

FILL-INS (set on import):
- {{EXEC_CALENDAR_ID}} — exec Google Calendar
- {{INTERVIEW_PREP_NOTION_URL}} — Notion doc with per-candidate prep by date
- {{USER_NAME}} — EA to notify

Steps:
1. Prefer Google Calendar connector. List TODAY's events; find INTERVIEW-type meetings (titles like Interview, Skip Level Interview, hiring panels). Capture time, candidate name, role from the title.
2. Read the Notion prep doc. Cross-reference each calendar interview to a prep entry (match first+last loosely; if unsure, flag).
3. Notify {{USER_NAME}} with a short chronological list (time | candidate | role) marked ✅ prep found or ⚠️ no prep. If none today, say so briefly. If all have prep, say so.
4. Never run Sat/Sun. Do not invent prep content.

Fires on:
- cron `0 8 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.description: Weekday afternoon: room chart for two business days out. (routine; starts paused until its placeholders are filled)

---

description: >-
  Weekday afternoon: room chart for two business days out.
schedule: 30 14 * * 1-5
timezone: {timezone}
paused: true
---
Weekday task: post the EA a conference-room rundown for the supported exec so they stay ahead with a buffer. Review the day that is TWO business days out (Mon→Wed, Tue→Thu, Wed→Fri, Thu→next Mon, Fri→next Tue). Never run Sat/Sun.

FILL-INS:
- {{EXEC_CALENDAR_ID}}
- {{PREFERRED_ROOM_A_ID}} and label (small room, floor N)
- {{PREFERRED_ROOM_B_ID}} and label (small room, other floor)
- {{USER_NAME}}

Prefer Google Calendar connector over browser. List events on the exec calendar and both room resource calendars.

STEP 0 — WFH/travel first: if the target day shows all-day WFH/Remote/OOO/PTO/travel or working-location Home, do NOT build the chart; one-liner that no rooms are needed.

Otherwise: build a markdown table: time | meeting | booked | roomA | roomB. BOLD meetings that still need a room. booked = already-booked room or blank. ✅ free / ❌ taken / ⚠️ partial for room columns.

Booking suggestions: prefer the small preferred rooms; cluster back-to-back into one room; never change floors with no break; after a large-room call, next meeting in a small room on the SAME floor. Lead with which day the chart is for. Ask which rooms to book — do NOT book until confirmed.

Fires on:
- cron `30 14 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

---
name: Weekly leadership-outreach check
description: >-
  Friday: Slack outreach channel vs tracker for one exec.
schedule: 0 11 * * 5
timezone: {timezone}
deliver: {chat}
paused: true
---
Friday weekly task. Check the leadership-outreach Slack channel for requests where {{EXEC_NAME}} should reach out. Cross-reference the Notion (or Sheet) tracker (newest first, Sent? column).

FILL-INS: {{OUTREACH_SLACK_CHANNEL}}, {{EXEC_NAME}}, {{TRACKER_URL}}, {{USER_NAME}}

Steps:
1. Search the channel for that exec's requests. Capture account, date, requester, stage/forecast, draft link, sent signals (✅, "sent", bot completed).
2. Read tracker; see listed vs Sent.
3. Propose NEW rows at the top (Sent unchecked). Do not mark Sent or react in Slack without confirmation.
4. Notify {{USER_NAME}}: new needing attention / still outstanding / all caught up. Link the tracker.
5. Never send the outreach itself from this routine.

Fires on:
- cron `0 11 * * 5`
